content.text:
Based on GitHub's docs, here's the design:

- **One repository per project** (private), under an **Organization** account (not personal account). Repos are the natural boundary — GitHub doesn't have granular "task-level" visibility, so isolation has to happen at the repo level.
- **Add each freelancer as an Outside Collaborator** on only the specific repo(s) containing their task — not as an Organization member. Outside collaborators "only have access to a specific repository," aren't org members, don't get the org's base permissions, and can't browse other repos (`managing-outside-collaborators/index.md`; `use-innersource.md`, "Make repositories discoverable").
- Give them the **Write** (or **Triage** if you just want them to comment/self-manage issues without pushing code) repository role — see `managing-repository-roles/repository-roles-for-an-organization.md`.
- Restrict who can *add* collaborators to org owners only, so freelancers can't invite others: `organizations/managing-organization-settings/setting-permissions-for-adding-outside-collaborators.md`.
- Practical pattern: repo naming like `customerA-projectX`, one GitHub Issue per task assigned to that freelancer, remove them as outside collaborator when the task/project ends (`removing-an-outside-collaborator-from-an-organization-repository.md`).
